tfn.s: The development plans were cancelled after the protests.

focus.note: Many verbs and nouns need one fixed small word after them. Learn the pair together, not just the first word.

items.s: Residents protested ____ the plans for the new car park.

tfn.s: The writer accepts that restrictions in a protected area can be necessary.
tfn.why: The text says such rules "can be genuinely necessary for conservation".

tfn.s: A local family who visits often is affected by a small charge more than a one-off holidaymaker.
tfn.why: The text says it is "the local family, not the holidaymaker, who pays it most often".

tfn.s: Most residents of the Arrábida area work in tourism.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say how many residents work in tourism.

tfn.s: The protesters believed the whole coastline had already been privatised.
tfn.why: The text says what they feared was "a future" of commercial control, and that opposition is "not the same as proof" of privatisation.

focus.note: Adjectives, verbs and nouns often take a fixed preposition. After the preposition, use a noun or an -ing form.

items.s: Whether the scheme works depends ____ how the money is spent.

Barriers protect the dunes ____ damage by large crowds.
Residents are interested ____ keeping the beach affordable.

Critics claimed the report had ____ public access with private ownership.
For a fragile dune system, strict limits on footfall may be ____, not merely desirable.
The two terms are not ____: each has a precise legal meaning.
Even after the redevelopment, longstanding residents hope to ____ their right to cross the dunes freely.
Planners tend to ____ how quickly a quiet cove can become overcrowded.

match.d: find a solution or method by thinking carefully

tfn.s: The writer suggests an identical restriction can be experienced as either protection or exclusion.
tfn.why: The text says restrictions may be "ecologically indispensable" yet can function "as a mechanism for discouraging ordinary visitors".

tfn.s: The text claims that earlier generations made money from the landscapes they preserved.
tfn.why: The text says they "preserved or shared them rather than cashing in".

tfn.s: Residents were consulted before the plans were drawn up.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text asks "who is consulted beforehand" but does not say whether anyone was.

tfn.s: The writer regards the protests as weak evidence about whether a coastal economy serves local people.
tfn.why: The text says: "the protests themselves may be the most useful evidence available."

tfn.s: A fixed fee is likely to be felt more heavily by regular local visitors than by one-off visitors.
tfn.why: The text says a fee seems small to someone visiting once, but a local family going back all summer "may see a very different cost".

focus.note: At this level the preposition is part of a fixed chunk, usually adjective plus preposition. Learn the whole chunk and its usual object.

items.s: Charging locals to reach their own shoreline would be tantamount ____ a tax on belonging.
Any plan to limit cars is fraught ____ political risk.
The scheme's approval was contingent ____ a satisfactory environmental review.
Critics say the profits were made ____ the expense of ordinary visitors.
The plan sits ____ stark contrast to the council's earlier promises.

speak.title: Role-play: a fee for the beach car park
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your council wants to charge a fee at the beach car park. The money will pay for cleaning and safety. Explain why, listen to the resident, and decide if you can offer anything.

b.text: You take your family to the beach about fifty times every summer. You think a fee is unfair for local people. Say why, and suggest a better idea.

phrases: I understand your point, but we've got to pay for the cleaning.
That's a lot of money for a family like ours.
What if local people got a discount?
I'm afraid we can't make an exception for everyone.
Who'd decide how the money's spent?
Let's try to find something that's fair for everybody.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you agree on a fee, and who was happiest with the result?
